title: Book One · Chapter 21: Too Many
story:
Jun tells his neighbour about the kite. His neighbour tells a girl in another class. On Wednesday, two more children ask Ronan for kites.

Both children wait for his answer. He likes that. He often asks other people for help. Now he can say yes to someone else.

"I can do a small one," he tells each of them.

The two families speak with Mum at pickup time. "The first kite still does not fly properly," she says. One parent says it is only a toy. The other child wants a kite for a younger sister and is very sure about it.

Mum looks at Ronan.

"How many kites did you promise to make?"

"Jun's. Then these two."

"And yours with Leo."

"That one's nearly done."

Mum doesn't take more money. "Please wait," she tells the families. "Ronan needs to check the work first." The two new families do not pay. Ronan has only said yes to them. She writes that down beside Jun's one coin.

At home, Ronan puts four little squares of paper on the table. One is for their own kite. Three are for the others.

Leo stands beside him. He has come to work on their flying line.

"Why didn't you tell me?"

"They asked today."

"You said yes today."

Ronan moves one square away from the others. "You only need to help with this."

"I know. But you keep saying we."

Ronan remembers his words at school. He did say we. He said it to both children. That made them think Leo would help. He did not ask Leo first.

"All right. I will say I."

Leo looks at the four squares. Then he takes out the string card.

They work quietly. Ronan wants to make the new paper shapes. Leo looks at the first kite. "Why does it turn down?" he asks. They cannot both use the table corner at once.

Mum comes to check. She asks Ronan to put everything ready for one extra kite in a row.

He lays out paper, one long strip, and one short strip. He needs more smooth bamboo strips. There is little paste in the pot. He counts the blue cloth strips. He has enough for one tail. He needs three.

"I need more than paper," he says.

"Yes," Mum says.

Dad can make a few more strips, but not tonight. He has a paid repair to finish at a neighbour's door. Mum needs her sewing space after dinner. Leo leaves before the light goes.

Ronan counts the evenings before class day on his fingers. He counted four kites. He did not count the evenings for the work.

"Could I do them all on Saturday?"

Mum sits beside him. "How long did the first shape take?"

"A long time."

"And that wasn't the whole kite."

He puts the squares in a small pile. They take hardly any space now. It feels unfair. Each square means a whole kite. He puts one finger on Jun's square. He has not made that kite yet. He has not started the other two.

"Can I say no after yes?"

"You can say, 'I cannot finish your kite.' Tell them soon. Then they can choose something else."

Ronan looks at the square for Jun. Jun asked, "What colour will the tail be?"

"I'll see tomorrow," he says.

Mum leaves the list on the table in front of him. Ronan leaves it on the table. He looks at it while Mum sews.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：counts＝数数；enough＝足够；paste＝浆糊；nearly＝差不多。

理解问题：

1. Ronan 总共答应了多少只风筝？
2. 纸上的清单为什么让他不再那么高兴？
